title: Trace a received good and answer it through conduct

sections.title: Understand the distinction
sections.body: Received goods can include knowledge, material labor and shared infrastructure. Acknowledging a limited good does not impose unlimited debt or erase harm. A response should fit the actual good and any existing agreement.

sections.title: Complete fictional practice material
sections.body: Complete fictional chain: volunteers wrote a cupboard guide, a librarian lent it until Friday 17:00, and Jo used its instruction to keep labels facing outward on Jo’s own shelf. The guide is intact. Jo has a Thursday 16:00 opportunity to return it to the staffed desk. No money, public thanks or future volunteer work was requested. One former volunteer also behaved hurtfully toward Jo; contact is not required.

sections.title: Work through the supplied case
sections.body: Trace at least three contributions and Jo’s own action. Choose a proportionate response, preserving the loan obligation and a boundary around unwanted contact.

sections.title: Try a different case before checking
sections.body: A helper says a freely given past favor now entitles them to private account access. Is this a gratitude obligation?

checks.title: Compare reasoning and review the supplied result
checks.body: Writing, lending and using are distinct contributions; the safe supplied skill is simply label orientation, not an invented repair technique. Returning the guide is an actual obligation; private remembrance or thanks can be optional. Later fiction: desk accepts the guide Thursday 16:00. Partial: thank generally but forget return. Incorrect: require reconciliation with the harmful person as payment for the useful text.
criteria: The chain includes others and one’s own contribution
Response fits the good and agreement

checks.title: Check the changed case
checks.body: No. Appreciation does not confer that access. Decline the new condition and keep any genuine separate agreement clear; receiving help does not surrender agency.
